Borrowed from Middle Iranian *tāk (“arch”); compare Middle Persian [script needed] (tʾg /⁠tāg⁠/, “arch”). Ultimately from the Proto-Indo-European root *teg- (“to cover; roof”), and akin to Latin toga (“garment”) and Ancient Greek στέγος (stégos, “roof”).

From طاق (ṭāq, “arch, doorway, opening in a wall”), from Middle Iranian *tāk (“arch”). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *teg-, and akin to Latin toga (“garment”) and Ancient Greek στέγος (stégos, “roof”).

parole.significato: carpet of fine piles, pile rug, nap
parole.testo: A Middle Iranian loanword, compare Persian تنبسه (tanbase).

From a Middle Iranian past participle āfrīd (“created”), originally an elliptic expression for *dīw afrīt (“demon’s creation”), or from the root ع ف ر (ʕ f r) related to “ash”, compare for the derivation type عَكْرُوت (ʕakrūt, “scoundrel”).
